metadata.title: The Amorphous Periodic Table of the Elements

categories.description: Forms continuous random networks (CRNs) via corner-sharing MX4 tetrahedra or mixed trigonal/tetrahedral polyhedra (CN=3-4) and acts as a metalloid solute center in bulk metallic glasses.
Provides low-coordination flexible bridges (-O-, -S-, -Se-, -N<, -F-, -Cl-, -Br-; CN=2-3) between cation polyhedra, enabling bond-angle disorder without cleaving covalent network connectivity.

Adopts 4-coordinate tetrahedral network coordination (e.g., AlO4-, GaO4-, BeF4, ZnCl4/ZnBr4, sp3 C4, VO4, MoO4, WO4, TiO4, InP4, CdGeAs2) when charge-compensated or covalently bonded; also stabilizes multicomponent metallic glasses.

Forms pyramidal, disphenoidal, octahedral, or antiprismatic glass polyhedra (TeO4, SbO3, BiO6, PbO4, TlSe3/TlSe4, NbO6, TaO6, OsO6, ZrF7/ZrO6, HfO6, FeO6, ThF8/ThF9) and/or serves as an early/late transition-metal matrix host in bulk metallic glasses.

Stabilizes five-fold symmetric icosahedral <0,0,12,0> (CN=12), polytetrahedral Frank-Kasper, and capped trigonal-prismatic clusters in metallic melts that frustrate periodic FCC/BCC/HCP crystallization.

Participates in multicomponent amorphous systems by modifying tetrahedral networks (creating non-bridging anions), charge-compensating [AlO4]-/[BO4]- tetrahedra, passivating dangling bonds (H), or providing large-atom topological cages in rare-earth/alkaline-earth/actinide glasses.

conversion_benchmarks.local_coordination: Quasi-tetrahedral/trigonal-prism SiAu9 p-d covalent clusters frustrating FCC packing
conversion_benchmarks.verification: Diffuse XRD halo; splat-quenching at 10^6 K/s; DSC crystallization peak
conversion_benchmarks.reference: KLEMENT, WILLENS & DUWEZ, Nature 187, 869 (1960) — "Non-crystalline Structure in Solidified Gold–Silicon Alloys"
conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: First melt-quenched metallic glass: introducing tetrahedral covalent Si lowers the eutectic temperature by ~700 K (to 636 K) and creates directional Au-Si p-d bonding that prevents FCC lattice nucleation.
conversion_benchmarks.structural_mechanism: First melt-quenched metallic glass: introducing tetrahedral covalent Si lowers the eutectic temperature by ~700 K (to 636 K) and creates directional Au-Si p-d bonding that prevents FCC lattice nucleation.

conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: Binary Pd-Ni alloys crystallize rapidly into FCC solid solutions; introducing 20 at.% P introduces directional p-d covalent prism motifs that reduce the critical cooling rate below 1 K/s.
conversion_benchmarks.structural_mechanism: Binary Pd-Ni alloys crystallize rapidly into FCC solid solutions; introducing 20 at.% P introduces directional p-d covalent prism motifs that reduce the critical cooling rate below 1 K/s.

conversion_benchmarks.reference: Hasegawa & Ray, Journal of Applied Physics 49, 4174 (1978) — "Iron-boron metallic glasses"
conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: Adding metalloid B (and Si) introduces short covalent-like Fe-B/Fe-Si bonds and trigonal-prismatic short-range order incompatible with translational BCC symmetry.

conversion_benchmarks.amorphous_system: FeGe, FeSi, CoSi, MnSi, FeGe3, Fe3Si7
conversion_benchmarks.local_coordination: Polytetrahedral M-Si / M-Ge p-d hybridized clusters (x~0.50) transitioning to tetrahedral Si4/Ge4 continuous random network (x<=0.30)

conversion_benchmarks.reference: Streubel et al., Advanced Materials 33, 2004830 (2021) — "Chiral Spin Textures in Amorphous Iron–Germanium Thick Films"
conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: While pure 3d metals (Fe, Co, Mn, Cr) crystallize into BCC/FCC/HCP lattices upon vapor deposition at 300 K, co-evaporating with tetrahedral Group-IV formers (Si, Ge) creates directional p-d covalent bonds that frustrate B20 crystal nucleation and convert non-magnetic Kondo insulator B20 FeSi into an itinerant amorphous ferromagnet (Hellman group, UC Berkeley).

conversion_benchmarks.reference: Streubel et al., Advanced Materials 33, 2004830 (2021) — "Chiral Spin Textures in Amorphous Iron–Germanium Thick Films"
conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: While pure 3d metals (Fe, Co, Mn, Cr) crystallize into BCC/FCC/HCP lattices upon vapor deposition at 300 K, co-evaporating with tetrahedral Group-IV formers (Si, Ge) creates directional p-d covalent bonds that frustrate B20 crystal nucleation and convert non-magnetic Kondo insulator B20 FeSi into an itinerant amorphous ferromagnet (Hellman group, UC Berkeley).

conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: Pure Te cannot be melt-quenched into a stable glass at room temperature, and stoichiometric GeTe crystallizes rapidly (CN=6 rocksalt). Introducing 15 at.% tetrahedral Ge (CN=4) locks Te chains into a Phillips-Thorpe optimally constrained 3D amorphous network.

conversion_benchmarks.amorphous_system: FeGe, FeSi, CoSi, MnSi, FeGe3, Fe3Si7
conversion_benchmarks.local_coordination: Polytetrahedral M-Si / M-Ge p-d hybridized clusters (x~0.50) transitioning to tetrahedral Si4/Ge4 continuous random network (x<=0.30)
conversion_benchmarks.verification: Diffuse XRD halo; HRTEM/SAED diffuse rings; Fe/Ge K-edge EXAFS; anomalous Hall & SQUID magnetometry
conversion_benchmarks.reference: Streubel et al., Advanced Materials 33, 2004830 (2021) — "Chiral Spin Textures in Amorphous Iron–Germanium Thick Films"
conversion_benchmarks.mechanism: While pure 3d metals (Fe, Co, Mn, Cr) crystallize into BCC/FCC/HCP lattices upon vapor deposition at 300 K, co-evaporating with tetrahedral Group-IV formers (Si, Ge) creates directional p-d covalent bonds that frustrate B20 crystal nucleation and convert non-magnetic Kondo insulator B20 FeSi into an itinerant amorphous ferromagnet (Hellman group, UC Berkeley).

conversion_benchmarks.added_element: Si or Ge tetrahedral host network (85-86 at.% Si/Ge)

conversion_benchmarks.reference: Zink et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 83, 2266 (1999) — "Large Magnetic Entropy in Giant Magnetoresistive Amorphous Gadolinium Silicon"
